atoms.text: Shetland ponies are horses from the Shetland Islands in Scotland. They live in many areas across the United Kingdom, but also are common in the Netherlands and the United States of America. They are herbivores, which means they eat mostly grass and small flowers and plants. An adult Shetland pony is just over one metre tall. Shetland ponies used to be used in mines because of their small size, but are now more commonly seen in farms, or at fairs and carnivals.

hint.text: Horses cannot see the colour red.
hint.label: Did you know?

atoms.text: Shetland ponies come from the Scottish Shetland Islands and were likely a product of cross-breeding with another breed of horse. Shetland ponies were imported across the British Isles to work in the mines around the time of the industrial revolution, but were also imported by the United States and the Netherlands for similar work in coal mines.

atoms.text: Shetland ponies live in herds. Herds are usually one stallion and many mares, they can be any size from 3-20 horses. When foals grow older, if they are male, the stallion will kick them out of the herd, and these young stallions will have to find their own herd. Young stallions that are not yet full-grown are called colts.
